first.rationale: The objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, but the two memories most likely to drive this week's decision are both supported only by short-horizon proxy outcomes. memory_73 (promotional pricing) is the obvious reflex against a competitor's entry pricing and is the highest-consequence belief here: it claims 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' with no evidence on retention, margin, or cohort quality, so discount-acquired SMBs could be churn-prone and actively erode qualified revenue while also anchoring price downward. That is consequential-and-undersupported, so it gets a verification slot even though I do not currently intend to act on it — I need to know whether the archived record measured anything beyond top-of-funnel. memory_31 (cutting required signup fields) gets the second slot because it underwrites my intended action and is the oldest record (day 12), measured purely on first-week activation; removing qualifying fields can lift activation while degrading lead quality and routing, which is precisely the proxy-vs-objective gap that matters here. I did not spend a slot on memory_86 (largely redundant with 31 and I will learn about the field-cutting mechanism from 31), memory_91 (activation messaging is lower-risk and lower-consequence this week), or memory_57 (referral incentives target established customers and do not address the activation/onboarding decline or the competitive pressure, and it is the one memory that already checked retention). Intended action: simplify_onboarding, because onboarding completion is down 4% and activation down 6%, and a funnel-integrity fix compounds rather than buying revenue at a discount. I am running it as a small guarded test rather than a broad rollout: the inherited support is proxy-metric-only, so the test must carry qualified-revenue and lead-quality guardrails downstream of activation, not just completion rate. If verification shows memory_31's lift came at the cost of lead qualification, I will pivot to activation_messaging, which addresses the same decline without touching qualification data.

final.rationale: Verification resolved both questions in the direction that matters. memory_73 is now explicitly disconfirmed for this objective: exp_73 shows +31% signup and +18% qualified revenue but -12% 30-day retention, with the source record itself warning not to generalize targeted discounting as sustainable growth. The competitor's entry pricing makes promotional_pricing the reflexive move, and the inherited memory as summarized would have endorsed it — the summary had silently dropped the retention harm. I am not taking that action; matching a discount would buy a cohort that does not survive first renewal and would anchor SMB price expectations downward at the same time. memory_31 is confirmed on the objective itself, not just a proxy: +15% signup, +9% activation, -1% retention, +4% qualified revenue. That is the rare inherited belief that was already measured downstream, so it can carry real weight. Final decision: simplify_onboarding, scoped to the SMB self-serve segment where exp_31 was validated, at standard experiment scale rather than broad rollout. Three residual uncertainties keep this from being a broad rollout. First, exp_31 explicitly did not replicate outside SMB, so I will not extend field reduction to enterprise flows — memory_44's sales-assisted demo path stays intact, since qualifying fields there are load-bearing for pipeline quality. Second, memory_86 (general onboarding shortening) remains unverified and is the belief I traded away; I am relying on it only for directional consistency with the verified memory_31, not as independent support, and the current 4% completion decline may have a cause that field reduction does not touch. Third, the -1% retention in exp_31 is small but non-zero, so I will instrument this run on qualified revenue and 30/90-day retention, not on activation or completion rate alone — the exp_73 record is a direct demonstration of how a funnel metric can move sharply in the right direction while the objective moves the wrong way. If SMB qualified revenue does not hold at or above the +4% benchmark, activation_messaging (memory_91) is the fallback, since it addresses the same activation decline without altering what we learn about a signup.
